context:
Goal: a builder spawned with no model runs Sonnet in every cloud session, with the fewest steps for you.
Problem (rule): the cloud drops the builder-model setting from your settings file, so your item 77 pick (a setup script, no pin) cannot work. The fix reverses that ruling or adds a paste per environment.
Based on (measured): the CLI code drops CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL from settings.json when the host manages the provider. A bare spawn ran Opus (Nov 1 01:22 CST).
Based on (ruling): item 77 (Oct 30 15:05 and 15:09 CDT): no pin in agents/builder.md. Record agent-model-cap, "No pin, and the ceiling is an ask".
Departs from: main (agent-model-cap: no pin; the variable comes from settings.json) — the model comes from a pin in agents/builder.md (a), or from each cloud environment's variables (b).

Your questions:
- Is the old A the same as a pin? Nearly, yes. Either way, a spawn that names no model runs Sonnet, and a spawn that names a model (a third-try Opus builder) wins. A pin is one line in one file in git, for every environment and machine at once. The old A lived in each cloud environment's settings, outside git: one paste per environment, and it can drift. You ruled out a pin so the setting could move builders, for example to Opus. In cloud that reason is gone: the cloud ignores that setting from your settings file, so it cannot move builders under either choice.
- Why was the old B a problem? It was a pin written as hook code: same effect as a pin, but as new code in the guard that reads every agent spawn, where a bug gives every agent the wrong model. It is dropped.

lastAnswer.note: i am completely confident that there was a period in time where sessions could and did CORRECTLy do like final rounds at a higher model like a round 3 builder on opus etc WITHOUT prompting me for approval and WITHOUT overusing opus incorrectly from the rules -- that's all i've been trying to implore, yet you seem rigid in your forms of what can actually occur?

options.gain: Works in every environment and on every machine at once, kept in git, nothing for you to paste.
options.how: One line, model: sonnet, in agents/builder.md, landed by PR; the lane rewrites agent-model-cap's no-pin paragraph.
options.label: Pin sonnet in the builder's agent file
options.lose: Reverses your item 77 ruling; moving builders to another model takes a one-line PR, not a setting.

options.gain: Keeps your no-pin record as written.
options.how: In a session of the environment: the environment menu in the title bar, then Edit, then Environment variables. Add CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=sonnet and CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL=sonnet.
options.label: You add two variables to each cloud environment

links.label: A session of this environment (menu in its title bar)

options.lose: One paste per environment; a new environment runs Opus builders until you paste; the value lives outside git. Unverified until a fresh session after the paste proves it.

options.how: No change; guard #899, which refuses a builder spawn that names no model, stays.
options.label: Keep naming the model on each spawn
options.lose: Every builder brief must name sonnet; a missed one is refused, and the session retries.

reply: You're right, and it still works today. A builder's third try on Opus runs with no prompt to you; every other agent stays on Sonnet. What allows it: hooks/guard.py opus_spawn_hit asks nothing for a builder whose brief carries 'Round 3 of 3' (builder_third_round), and a guard test pins it. Still asks, by your rules: a reviewer's round 3 on Opus, and Opus on any agent without that marker. The cloud gap touches only a builder spawned with no model named: guard #899 refuses that spawn, the session names sonnet and retries, so nothing runs Opus by mistake. The question is dropped; your no-pin ruling (item 77) stands.
title: The cloud ignores the builder model in your settings file. Where should it come from?
why: It gives the same effect as b with no paste, and in cloud the reason for no pin no longer holds.
